To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

human cytosol and porcine and human amniatic fluid proteins increase the voltage dependence (i.e. the slope of the voltage dependence of conductance) of human type- 1 porin reconstitution in planar phospho-lipid bilayers and that the regulatory activity is due to the presence specific proteins in the investigated samples.

human cytosol and porcine and human amniolic fluid contain proteins that inhibit human type-1 (porin) in a potential dependent manner, and that the inhibitory activity of these proteins is due to the specific molecular properties of the proteins and is not due to the presence anionic charge alone.
human cytosolic and amniotic proteins increase the voltage dependence (inhibitory) of porin reconstitu- ted into planar phospholippid membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the physiological control of porin in plasma membranes and the role of the channel as a mediator of ion transport across the cell membrane.
the identification of regulatory proteins which are involved in the voltage-dependent regulation of human type- 1 porin.
the identification of regulatory factors for the human type-1 voltage-dependent anion channel (VDAC).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented data are the first to show the regulation of the voltage dependence of a channel protein by specific proteins of cytosol.
the observed regulatory activity of cytosol proteins on porin is due to a specific molecular interaction of the regulatory proteins with the channel.

the observed regulatory activity of the cytosolic and amniotic proteins on porin is due to a direct interaction of the channel with the proteins, but not due to a change of the lipid environment of the membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the voltage dependence of porins can be modulated by proteins of cytosol or amniotic fluid.
porin is regulated by heat-stable proteins of cytosol, which are able to change the voltage dependence of the porin channel in a voltage-dependent manner.
porin can be regulated in the plasma membrane by specific proteins of cytosol or amniotic fluid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activity of porin is not only controlled by membrane voltage but is also regulated by specific heat-stable proteins in the cell.
the voltage dependence of the channel can be altered in the presence of certain proteins.
the channel properties of porin are regulated by proteins in human and porcincytoplasm, which may be involved in the regulation of the channel activity in the cell membrane.
